title: Task Brief authoring convention and Task Explorer
summary: 160 authored Task Briefs explain all 284 imported source entries. The catalogue lists shared tasks once, with case-specific context underneath, separate assistance conditions and expandable provenance. Six briefs have native/source-derived examples; externally packaged case inventories and additional visuals remain incomplete.

links.label: Published source inventory and coverage gaps
Public sample download, access and visual receipts

decision_provenance: 2026-09-21 user answers: samples now and all tasks eventually; technically literate audience without specialist medical knowledge; existing and proposed tasks with clear draft marking. Other architecture and visual recommendations are by the assistant and await decisions. Later user response “all your rec” accepted shared definition briefs with case indexes, input-first reference reveals, reusable skill plus repository rulebook/template, and separately authoritative executable contracts. User subsequently requested searching and downloading necessary samples. This authorized bounded public data acquisition, not model trials. The user later requested complete brief coverage, then flagged repetitive badges, shared previews and metadata. The assistant refactored presentation to shared task rows with concise case differences and expandable provenance.
reopen_when: When a source revision or task condition changes, a missing case inventory becomes available, or reader feedback demonstrates a needed format change.
